verdict.rationale: Hands-on community reports describe the server-side architecture the story asks for: SDKs download all flags in the project on connection, then stream changes over SSE, so flag checks add no network latency. LaunchDarkly's own pages in the pack only list 13 server-side SDKs and the Relay Proxy streaming connection, and Big Segments are noted to fetch live from Redis before caching. missing for 10: first-party documentation of in-process local evaluation from a cached ruleset, evidence of microsecond-level evaluation latency, and fully local evaluation for Big Segments.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, my server SDKs evaluate flags locally from a cached ruleset — microsecond decisions with no network call per flag check

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly clients download all flags in the project on connection, then stream changes.
Its server-sent events streaming adds no extra latency for flag checks.
30 idiomatic SDKs 13 client-side, 13 server-side, and 4 edge SDKs.
It connects to the LaunchDarkly streaming API and proxies that connection to clients within your organization’s network.
